---
title: "Writing Custom Parameter Functions"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, .quiet = TRUE)

# Shared dataset
d_conc <- as.data.frame(Theoph) |> rename(time = Time, subject = Subject)
d_dose <- Theoph |> as.data.frame() |>
  group_by(Subject) |>
  summarise(dose = Dose[1] * Wt[1], .groups = "drop") |>
  rename(subject = Subject) |>
  mutate(time = 0)

o_conc <- PKNCAconc(d_conc, conc ~ time | subject)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(d_dose, dose ~ time | subject, route = "extravascular")
```

## The parameter registry

Every NCA parameter that PKNCA can compute is **registered** in an internal registry via `add.interval.col()`. When you request `auclast = TRUE` in an interval, PKNCA looks up the registered function for `auclast` and calls it with the right arguments.

You can extend the registry with your own parameters — new functions that compute anything derivable from concentrations, times, doses, or other already-computed parameters. See also the package vignette [Writing PKNCA Parameter Functions](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v80-writing-parameter-functions.html).

```{r}
# Number of parameters registered by default
length(get.interval.cols())
```

---

## Anatomy of `add.interval.col()`

```r
add.interval.col(
  name           = "my.param",          # column name used in the intervals data frame
  FUN            = "pk.calc.my.param",  # function name as a character string, or NA
  values         = c(FALSE, TRUE),      # allowed values in intervals (FALSE = skip, TRUE = compute)
  unit_type      = "time",              # units category (required; see below)
  pretty_name    = "My parameter",      # human-readable label for summary tables
  depends        = NULL,                # other parameters that must be computed first
  desc           = "What it does",      # one-line description; SDTM limit 40 characters
  formalsmap     = list(),              # list(<your function arg> = <data or parameter name>)
  FUN_sparse     = NA,                  # sparse-PK estimator (function name), if any
  formalsmap_sparse = list(),           # formalsmap for FUN_sparse
  datatype       = "interval",          # only "interval" is supported; the others error
  pptestcd_cdisc = "MYPARAM",           # CDISC PPTESTCD code (defaults to name)
  pptest_cdisc   = "My Parameter",      # CDISC PPTEST label (defaults to desc)
  formula        = NULL,                # LaTeX expression, for documentation
  formula_note   = NULL,                # note on the formula; also the PPANMETH fallback
  tier           = "uncommon",          # "common" or "uncommon"
  selection      = NULL                 # list(concept=, route=, dosing=, secondary=)
)
```

**Key rule:** `FUN` must be a **character string** (the function name), not a function object.

What each argument does, as of PKNCA 0.13.0:

| Argument | Notes |
|---|---|
| `name` | A non-empty string. Names ending in `_ref` and the name `interval_id` are reserved for the reference-interval linkage columns (see [Example 4](#example-4-a-parameter-that-needs-another-interval)) and are an error. |
| `FUN` | The calculation function's name, or `NA` for a parameter that is filled in as one column of another parameter's data-frame result, or that only a `FUN_sparse` estimator calculates. |
| `unit_type` | Required; one of the values listed below. |
| `desc` | Since 0.13.0, a description longer than 40 characters (the SDTM limit) is still registered but gives a warning. |
| `formalsmap` | Maps your function's arguments to data, parameters, constants (`I()`), or reference-interval values (`pknca_ref()`); see [below](#the-formalsmap-argument). |
| `FUN_sparse`, `formalsmap_sparse` (≥ 0.13.0) | A second calculation function used when the data are sparse; see [Example 5](#example-5-a-sparse-only-parameter). |
| `pptestcd_cdisc`, `pptest_cdisc` (≥ 0.13.0) | The codes used by `as.data.frame(out_format = "cdisc")`. Each is a single string, a list with one element `route` holding a named list by route (`list(route = list(extravascular = "CLF/FO", intravascular = "CLO"))`), or a list of exactly the elements `dense` and `sparse`; anything else is an error. |
| `formula`, `formula_note` (≥ 0.13.0) | Documentation of the calculation. When the calculation function sets no `"method"` attribute, `formula_note` is reported in the `PPANMETH` column. |
| `tier`, `selection` (≥ 0.13.0) | Classification used by automatic interval selection and reported by `pknca_parameter_table()`. A custom parameter is `"uncommon"` by default, so it is calculated only when requested by name. |
| `sparse` | Retired (≥ 0.13.0). `sparse = TRUE` is an error; an explicit `sparse = FALSE` is accepted and does nothing. Register a sparse-only parameter with `FUN = NA` and `FUN_sparse` instead. |

### Available `unit_type` values

`"unitless"`, `"fraction"`, `"%"`, `"count"`, `"time"`, `"inverse_time"`, `"amount"`, `"amount_dose"`, `"amount_time"`, `"conc"`, `"conc_dosenorm"`, `"dose"`, `"volume"`, `"auc"`, `"aumc"`, `"auc_dosenorm"`, `"aumc_dosenorm"`, `"clearance"`, `"renal_clearance"`, `"renal_clearance_dosenorm"`

---

## The `formalsmap` argument

Each `formalsmap` entry has the form `<your function's argument> = "<PKNCA data name>"` — the **names** of the list must be your function's formal arguments, and the **values** are the PKNCA data or parameter names that supply them. For example, PKNCA registers `mrt.obs` with `formalsmap = list(auc = "aucinf.obs", aumc = "aumcinf.obs")`: the computed `aucinf.obs` value is passed to the function's `auc` argument.

Values available in a `formalsmap` (the full list is in `?add.interval.col`):

| `formalsmap` value | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `"conc"`, `"time"` | Concentrations and times for the current interval (times start at 0 at the interval start) |
| `"dose"`, `"time.dose"`, `"duration.dose"`, `"route"` | Dose amounts, times, durations, and route for the current interval |
| `"volume"`, `"duration.conc"` | Sample volume and collection duration (urine and feces) |
| `"start"`, `"end"` | Interval start and end times (`end` may be `Inf`) |
| `"options"` | The `PKNCA.options()` in effect for the calculation |
| `"conc.group"`, `"time.group"`, `"dose.group"`, ... | The same inputs for the whole group rather than the interval |
| `"conc.sparse"`, `"time.sparse"`, `"subject"`, ... (≥ 0.13.0) | The pooled individual samples of sparse data (`NULL` for dense data) |
| *(any parameter name)* | The computed value of that parameter in the current interval (list it in `depends`) |
| `I(<value>)` (≥ 0.13.0) | A constant, passed to the function unchanged |
| `pknca_ref("<parameter>")` (≥ 0.13.0) | The value of that parameter in the reference interval |
| `NULL` | Drop the argument from the call so that it keeps its default |

If your function argument names **exactly match** PKNCA's standard names, `formalsmap` can be omitted or left empty. An argument whose name matches a registered parameter is filled from that parameter when it is not in the `formalsmap`, so map such an argument to `NULL` if your parameter does not use it.

---

## Example 1: derived from other parameters

A parameter that divides two already-computed parameters. Use `depends` to declare what must be computed first (shown here without `formalsmap` because the function's argument names match the parameter names). Requesting `exposure.ratio` alone is enough: PKNCA calculates everything in `depends` first, and `get.parameter.deps("exposure.ratio", recursive = TRUE)` lists what it is ultimately calculated from.

```{r}
# Exposure ratio: AUClast / Cmax  (units: time, since AUC/conc = time × conc/conc = time)
pk.calc.exposure.ratio <- function(auclast, cmax) {
  auclast / cmax
}

add.interval.col(
  name        = "exposure.ratio",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.exposure.ratio",
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "time",
  pretty_name = "Exposure ratio (AUClast / Cmax)",
  desc        = "AUClast divided by Cmax",
  depends     = c("auclast", "cmax"),
  formula     = "\\frac{AUC_{last}}{C_{max}}"
)
```

```{r}
o_nca_er <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = data.frame(
  start          = 0, end = Inf,
  auclast        = TRUE,
  cmax           = TRUE,
  exposure.ratio = TRUE
)))

as.data.frame(o_nca_er) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "exposure.ratio")) |>
  select(subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(check = auclast / cmax) |>
  arrange(subject)
```

---

## Example 2: computed from raw concentration-time data, with a constant

A parameter that accesses `conc` and `time` directly. PKNCA passes the raw vectors from the concentration data. No `depends` needed. The target time is passed as a constant with `I()` (≥ 0.13.0): without `I()`, `2` would be looked up as a data or parameter name instead of being passed as a value. The same function could be registered again as `c.4h` with `time.out = I(4)`.

```{r}
# Concentration at a fixed time (interpolated)
pk.calc.conc.at <- function(conc, time, time.out) {
  interp.extrap.conc(conc = conc, time = time, time.out = time.out)
}

add.interval.col(
  name           = "c.2h",
  FUN            = "pk.calc.conc.at",
  values         = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type      = "conc",
  pretty_name    = "Concentration at 2 h",
  desc           = "Interpolated concentration at 2 h",
  depends        = NULL,
  formalsmap     = list(conc = "conc", time = "time", time.out = I(2)),
  pptestcd_cdisc = "C2H",
  pptest_cdisc   = "Concentration at 2 h",
  formula_note   = "Interpolated with interp.extrap.conc()"
)
```

```{r}
o_nca_c2 <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf, c.2h = TRUE
)))

as.data.frame(o_nca_c2) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "c.2h") |>
  select(subject, PPORRES, PPANMETH) |>
  arrange(subject)
```

`pk.calc.conc.at()` sets no `"method"` attribute, so `PPANMETH` falls back to the registered `formula_note`. The CDISC codes appear in the CDISC output:

```{r}
as.data.frame(o_nca_c2, out_format = "cdisc") |>
  filter(subject == "1") |>
  select(subject, pknca_parameter, PPTESTCD, PPTEST, PPORRES)
```

---

## Example 3: multiple related parameters sharing a dependency

When computing several related quantities (e.g. early AUC, late AUC, and their ratio), register each as its own function. The late-AUC and fraction functions read the already-computed `auclast` dependency.

```{r}
pk.calc.auc.early <- function(conc, time) {
  t_idx <- time <= 4
  if (sum(t_idx) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  pk.calc.auc.last(conc[t_idx], time[t_idx])
}

pk.calc.auc.late <- function(conc, time, auclast) {
  t_idx <- time <= 4
  if (sum(t_idx) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  auclast - pk.calc.auc.last(conc[t_idx], time[t_idx])
}

pk.calc.auc.early.frac <- function(conc, time, auclast) {
  t_idx <- time <= 4
  if (sum(t_idx) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  pk.calc.auc.last(conc[t_idx], time[t_idx]) / auclast
}

add.interval.col(
  name        = "auc.early",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.auc.early",
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "auc",
  pretty_name = "AUC to last sample <= 4h",
  desc        = "AUC to the last sample at or before 4 h",
  depends     = NULL,
  formalsmap  = list(conc = "conc", time = "time")
)

add.interval.col(
  name        = "auc.late",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.auc.late",
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "auc",
  pretty_name = "AUC 4h to last",
  desc        = "AUC from 4 h to last sample",
  depends     = "auclast",
  formalsmap  = list(conc = "conc", time = "time", auclast = "auclast")
)

add.interval.col(
  name        = "auc.early.fraction",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.auc.early.frac",
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "fraction",
  pretty_name = "Early AUC fraction",
  desc        = "Fraction of AUClast in the first 4 h",
  depends     = "auclast",
  formalsmap  = list(conc = "conc", time = "time", auclast = "auclast")
)
```

These functions return values from `pk.calc.auc.last()`, which carry a `"method"` attribute ("AUC: lin up/log down" with the default `auc.method`); the attribute survives the subtraction and division, so `pk.nca()` reports it in the `PPANMETH` column of these custom parameters too. Return `as.numeric()` of a value if its method should not be reported.

> **Note:** One function *can* populate several output parameters at once by returning a **one-row data frame** whose column names are registered parameter names — `pk.nca()` saves every column of the returned data frame. A data frame whose names and values do not pair up (for example, one with zero rows) is an error naming the function (≥ 0.13.0). This is exactly how `pk.calc.half.life()` populates `half.life`, `lambda.z`, `r.squared`, and the other half-life diagnostics. Each output still needs its own `add.interval.col()` registration: register the function on the primary parameter, and register the other columns with `FUN = NA` plus a `depends` on the primary (`formalsmap` may not be given when `FUN = NA`). The one-function-per-parameter pattern shown above is the simpler option when each output is cheap to compute.

```{r}
o_nca_split <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = data.frame(
  start              = 0, end = Inf,
  auclast            = TRUE,
  auc.early          = TRUE,
  auc.late           = TRUE,
  auc.early.fraction = TRUE
)))

as.data.frame(o_nca_split) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "auc.early", "auc.late", "auc.early.fraction")) |>
  select(subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  arrange(subject)
```

The same split can be computed by **one** multi-output function returning a one-row data frame:

```{r}
pk.calc.auc.split <- function(conc, time, auclast) {
  t_idx <- time <= 4
  early <- if (sum(t_idx) < 2) NA_real_ else pk.calc.auc.last(conc[t_idx], time[t_idx])
  data.frame(auc.early.df = early, auc.late.df = auclast - early)
}

add.interval.col(
  name        = "auc.early.df",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.auc.split",  # computes BOTH auc.early.df and auc.late.df
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "auc",
  pretty_name = "AUC 0-4h (multi-output)",
  desc        = "AUC from 0 to 4 h (multi-output)",
  depends     = "auclast",
  formalsmap  = list(conc = "conc", time = "time", auclast = "auclast")
)

add.interval.col(
  name        = "auc.late.df",
  FUN         = NA,                   # populated by pk.calc.auc.split via auc.early.df
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "auc",
  pretty_name = "AUC 4h to last (multi-output)",
  desc        = "AUC from 4 h to last (multi-output)",
  depends     = "auc.early.df"
)

o_nca_multi <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  auclast = TRUE, auc.early.df = TRUE, auc.late.df = TRUE
)))

as.data.frame(o_nca_multi) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "auc.early.df", "auc.late.df")) |>
  select(subject, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  arrange(subject)
```

## Example 4: a parameter that needs another interval

Some parameters compare two intervals — bioavailability, renal clearance, and the built-in `ratio.*` parameters. Wrapping a `formalsmap` value in `pknca_ref()` (≥ 0.13.0) takes that argument from the **reference** interval instead of the current one. The intervals then link the two rows: the reference row gets an `interval_id`, and the row calculating the parameter names it in a `<parameter>_ref` column. Here a custom parameter subtracts the reference interval's `aucint.last` from the current one's:

```{r}
pk.calc.aucint.change <- function(aucint.last, aucint_reference) {
  aucint.last - aucint_reference
}

add.interval.col(
  name        = "aucint.change",
  FUN         = "pk.calc.aucint.change",
  values      = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type   = "auc",
  pretty_name = "AUCint change from reference",
  desc        = "AUCint,last minus reference AUCint,last",
  depends     = "aucint.last",
  formalsmap  = list(aucint_reference = pknca_ref("aucint.last"))
)

intervals_linked <- data.frame(
  start               = c(0, 8),
  end                 = c(8, 24),
  interval_id         = c("first8h", NA),
  aucint.last         = TRUE,
  aucint.change       = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  aucint.change_ref   = c(NA, "first8h")
)

o_nca_linked <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals_linked))

as.data.frame(o_nca_linked) |>
  filter(subject %in% c("1", "2")) |>
  select(subject, start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES, PPANMETH) |>
  arrange(subject, start)
```

A `pknca_ref()` in the `formalsmap` makes the parameter *secondary* (calculated after every interval, from the results), so its function may take only parameter values — every argument comes either from the reference interval through `pknca_ref()` or from a parameter of the current interval listed in `depends`. The secondary row's `PPANMETH` names the reference interval. Requesting, linking, and automatically deriving reference intervals are covered in the [secondary parameters chapter](secondary-parameters.qmd) and the [Secondary Parameters vignette](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v09-secondary-parameters.html).

---

## Example 5: a sparse-only parameter

A parameter registered with `FUN = NA` and a `FUN_sparse` (≥ 0.13.0) is calculated only for sparse data, from the pooled individual samples. `formalsmap_sparse` replaces `formalsmap` for that function and can name the sparse inputs, such as `subject`. (Before 0.13.0 this was `sparse = TRUE`, which is now an error.)

```{r}
pk.calc.n.subjects <- function(subject) {
  length(unique(subject))
}

add.interval.col(
  name              = "n.subjects",
  FUN               = NA,
  FUN_sparse        = "pk.calc.n.subjects",
  values            = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  unit_type         = "count",
  pretty_name       = "Subjects contributing samples",
  desc              = "Number of subjects with samples",
  formalsmap_sparse = list(subject = "subject")
)

# Two samples from each of six animals
d_sparse <- data.frame(
  animal = rep(1:6, each = 2),
  time   = c(0.5, 4, 2, 8, 12, 0.5, 24, 2, 4, 12, 8, 24),
  conc   = c(2, 3, 4, 2.5, 3.6, 2, 1.5, 1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.6, 0.2)
)
o_conc_sparse <- PKNCAconc(d_sparse, conc ~ time | animal, sparse = TRUE)

o_nca_sparse <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc_sparse, intervals = data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24, n.subjects = TRUE
)))
as.data.frame(o_nca_sparse) |>
  select(start, end, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
```

Requesting `n.subjects` for dense data is an error, and `pknca_parameter_table()` reports the parameter as sparse:

```{r}
pknca_parameter_table(c("exposure.ratio", "c.2h", "aucint.change", "n.subjects")) |>
  select(parameter, concept, tier, sparse, secondary)
```

A custom parameter whose concept cannot be derived (here `exposure.ratio`, `c.2h`, and `n.subjects`) has `NA` for `concept`: it is calculated normally when requested by name, but it is never selected automatically. Declare one with `selection = list(concept = ...)` (see `pknca_concepts()` for the vocabulary) or with `pknca_concept()` on the calculation function. `aucint.change` takes its concept from its dependency and is secondary because of its `pknca_ref()`.

A parameter with both `FUN` and `FUN_sparse` uses `FUN_sparse` for sparse data and `FUN` for dense data; one with only `FUN` is calculated on the arithmetic-mean profile for sparse data. Sparse analyses are covered in the [sparse NCA chapter](sparse.qmd).

---

## Inspecting registered parameters

```{r}
# Confirm your parameter is registered
cols <- get.interval.cols()
cat("exposure.ratio registered:", "exposure.ratio" %in% names(cols), "\n")
cat("c.2h registered:          ", "c.2h" %in% names(cols), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Inspect registration details
str(cols[["exposure.ratio"]])
```

---

## Custom summary statistics for your parameter

After registering the parameter, set a custom summary rule with `PKNCA.set.summary()`:

```{r}
PKNCA.set.summary(
  "exposure.ratio",
  description = "geometric mean [CV%]",
  point  = PKNCA::geomean,
  spread = PKNCA::geocv
)

summary(pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, exposure.ratio = TRUE
))))
```

The vignette's [summary section](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v80-writing-parameter-functions.html#tell-pknca-how-to-summarize-the-parameter) covers the same registration.

---

## Important notes

- **Registration is session-scoped.** Custom parameters registered with `add.interval.col()` persist for the life of your R session. Re-run registration code in each session (e.g. in your analysis script or package).
- **`FUN` must be a character string.** Passing a function object causes an error.
- **`depends` controls evaluation order.** List all parameters your function reads. PKNCA resolves the dependency graph and ensures they are computed before your function is called.
- **Functions must be in scope** when `pk.nca()` runs. Define them in the global environment or in a package loaded before calling `pk.nca()`.
- **Keep `desc` to 40 characters or fewer** if the results may go into an SDTM submission; longer descriptions warn.
